page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v5 is an EASv5-series memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor executing on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores operating with two threads per core at clock frequencies up to 3.525 GHz. Cache topology features a 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions are supported via AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, while vector execution includes standard AVX and FMA, omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

The instance features 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio typical of memory-intensive infrastructure. It provides no bundled local storage, requiring attached Azure Premium Storage volumes for OS and data persistence. Dedicated GPU hardware is absent. Synthetic memory throughput tests reflect an uncached large-block read speed of 77.88 GB/sec and a write speed of 44.48 GB/sec, alongside a cached small-block read speed of 2075.82 GB/sec.

Benchmark assessments highlight strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng evaluations, ranking within the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance remains balanced, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 12833.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 38185.8. In memory-intensive services, the platform sustained 32.43 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks. Text generation using small language models remains in the top 25 percent, but CPU-only inference degrades sharply when processing large 70-billion parameter models.

Qualitatively, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio provides cost efficiency for memory-constrained applications that do not require specialized hardware accelerators. By offloading persistence to external storage networks, resources remain concentrated on memory capacity and multi-threaded computation. The server fits high-capacity caching deployments such as Redis, relational databases like PostgreSQL and MySQL, enterprise ERP systems, and memory-bound ETL pipelines.

Local storage is not included, and the instance features no GPU accelerators, relying on remote Premium Storage for disk operations. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng evaluations, alongside standard multi-core compute capability, scoring 12833.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 38185.8 in PassMark. Memory operations reached 32.43 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. The resource profile provides balanced qualitative efficiency for memory-heavy deployments, fitting enterprise transactional databases, distributed in-memory caches, and memory-constrained analytics pipelines.
